title: Weekly Coaching — Week of Nov 2–6, 2026
html:
One bad day broke the floor. Now $745 is the ceiling.

Here’s what I’m seeing. The week started calm, rallied on Wednesday after the midterms, then fell apart Thursday in the worst day since April 2025. SPY finished the week down 2.7%. The travel names held up and the AI names did not. Let’s grade our calls, then set up next week.

The one thing

SPY’s old floor at $744–745 is now its ceiling. The real floor is $722–728, where the 200-day sits. Until SPY closes back above $745, keep trades small and favor the names that held up.

SPY closed Friday at $735.29 (the S&P 500 at 7,376.86). Thursday it fell 4.4% after Democrats won Congress on a platform that includes limits on data centers. Chip earnings from Qualcomm and Arm also disappointed. The chip ETF fell about 11% that day. Friday’s bounce was small: SPY reached $742.21 and stalled just under the old floor. A hot jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 70,000 expected) raised the odds of a December rate hike to about 77%. A close back above $745 says the scare is over. A close below $722 says the uptrend is broken and cash is a position.

Grading last week’s calls

  • Week Ahead: watch $752, then $743–745. A break means defense, toward $734 then $722. — Right. The map worked. SPY held $752 Monday and Tuesday (lows $751.60 and $752.39), then broke $743–745 on Thursday and closed at $733.00, right at our $734 downside marker. I didn’t expect Wednesday’s rally to $775.64 first, though.
  • Nov 4: holding $762 means the pullback is likely over. — Wrong. That was the worst call of the week. SPY gave up $762 the very next day and fell 4.4%. The lesson: one strong day after an election is not a trend. I leaned on it too fast.
  • HLT Dec 18 $380 call. Enter on a close above $364.50. — Right. It triggered Monday (close $364.71). HLT made a record $381.34 on Thursday and closed the week at $370.45, up 3.8% while SPY fell. That contract now trades near $1,025, up from about $760 when it triggered.
  • DAL Dec 18 $85 call. Enter on a close above $85.40. — Right. It triggered Wednesday (close $89.24). DAL pulled back with the market Thursday but never closed under the $80.90 stop. It finished up 8.8% for the week. The $85 call is now about $655, up from about $440.
  • NVDA: a put on a close below $200; calls only above $210.94. — Half right. Waiting on calls saved us. The miss: I cancelled the put idea on Tuesday. Wednesday NVDA closed at $200.13, 13 cents above the trigger, then fell 9% Thursday. The trigger was right; dropping it early was my mistake.
  • XOM: buy calls on a pullback to $176, later changed to “avoid”. — Right. Moving to avoid was right. The pullback reached $177 and kept going down to $163.51. XOM fell 11.4% for the week as Brent dropped below $100.
  • BA Dec 18 $170 put after a failed rally near $183–185. — No trade. The rally topped at $179.19 and never reached our zone, so we never entered. BA ended the week up 1.1%. Nothing lost; patience cost nothing here.
  • RCL: buy a dip to $307–308, later $324.55, that closes back above. — Too strict. RCL never dipped to $307. Thursday it closed at $322.73, under $324.55, so the rule kept us out. It finished up 6.5%. Strict rules sometimes leave money on the table, and that’s acceptable.
  • Nov 5: skip chip puts at peak fear. — Right. Friday chips bounced hard: AMD +11.0%, SMCI +6.2%, MU +5.1%. Puts bought Thursday’s close lost money fast.

The week in one picture — SPY ladder

  • $781.62 — Oct 6 record high
  • $763–765 — Ceiling · 61.8% + 20 & 50-day
  • $751–757 — 38.2–50% of the Oct–Nov drop
  • $744–745 — The line · old floor, two 23.6% Fibs
  • NOW $735.29
  • $732.4–732.7 — Shelf · Nov 5 low + 1.382 ext
  • $722–728 — Big floor · 200-day + 38.2% + 1.618
  • $703.87 — 50% of the Mar–Oct run

How I read it: Two Fib levels from different swings land at $744–745. One is the 23.6% retracement of the big Mar 30 → Oct 6 run ($626.11 → $781.62). The other is the 23.6% of the recent Oct 6 → Nov 5 drop ($781.62 → $732.71). That zone was our floor all week. It broke Thursday, and Friday’s rally stopped at $742.21, just under it. Below us, three things meet at $722–728: the 200-day ($727.65), the 38.2% of the big run ($722.22) and the 1.618 extension of the Oct 6 → Oct 30 → Nov 4 swing ($725.06). That is where buyers should show up. What changes my view: a close above $745 turns me neutral-to-bullish; a close below $722 turns me defensive.

Themes

  • Travel & asset-light hotels (HLT · ABNB · RCL · DAL · BA) — bull 82/100. Winning. ABNB +15.6%, DAL +8.8%, RCL +6.5%, HLT +3.8% in a down week. BA is the laggard.
  • Defensive rotation (KO) — bull 70/100. KO touched a 52-week high ($97.39) Thursday. Staples and health care held up.
  • Mega-cap consumer & cloud (AAPL · AMZN · GOOGL) — mid 52/100. Split. AMZN +7.9% on the week; AAPL flat; GOOGL still in a downtrend.
  • Oil shock / Iran (XOM · XLE · USO) — mid 40/100. Cracking. XLE −12% for the week even after tanker attacks near Hormuz. Brent slipped below $100.
  • Rates & a hiking Fed (TLT · IWM) — mid 38/100. Hike odds near 77% for December. TLT steady at $81.92; small caps (IWM) −2%.
  • Defense (LMT · BA) — bear 32/100. LMT fell 11% this week. Last Sunday’s overbought warning was right.
  • Musk complex (TSLA · SPCX) — bear 30/100. TSLA −10.4%; Musk said Cybertruck output winds down next year.
  • AI infrastructure capex (NVDA · MU · AMD · SMH · DRAM · SMCI · DELL · BE) — bear 18/100. Losing. SMH −11.2%, MU −22%, DELL −22.6%. Goldman thinks about 45% of planned US data-center capacity could face limits.
  • AI vs software (NOW · PLTR) — bear 14/100. Still losing. NOW made a new low ($100.55); PLTR −12.9%.

Why these four: HLT and DAL are live plays near their triggers, NVDA is the weak AI name at a Fib decision point with earnings ahead, and BA is your current ideas’ downside setup sitting on its trigger.

  • Watching: Trigger: a close above $381.34, or another hold of $362–364.50 that closes back over $370. Out on a close below $359.41. Targets $385.93, then $399.73.

What the big banks think

  • Goldman Sachs (Ben Snider): 8,000 (≈ $797 SPY). Raised from 7,600; sees earnings, not higher valuations, doing the work.
  • Citi (Scott Chronert): 8,100 (≈ $807 SPY). Highest on the Street. In September Chronert himself called it “overly ambitious.”
  • BofA (Savita Subramanian): 7,100 (≈ $708 SPY). Street low. She has warned of “too many red flags” for months.
  • JPMorgan: 8,000 (≈ $797 SPY). Raised earlier this year on strong earnings and AI spending.
  • Morgan Stanley (Mike Wilson): 8,000 (≈ $797 SPY). Base case 8,000 (Nov 2 note); flagged 7,100–7,200 as a possible downside area.

With the S&P at 7,376.86, four of five banks still see 8% upside by Dec 31, with eight weeks left. That’s a big ask. I give more weight to Morgan Stanley’s 7,100–7,200 downside area, which lines up with SPY near $708–718.

Hedge funds & flows

Thursday was a crowded exit. Goldman says tech-focused hedge funds lost more than 4% that day, which erased their gains for the year. They had cut risk before the election, chased Wednesday’s rally, then sold the same big tech names a day later. Traders bought a record 11.2 million put contracts and the VIX, Wall Street’s fear gauge, jumped about 70% to 28. Friday it eased to 25.6. Forced selling like this usually ends fast. A real bottom needs buyers to show up, not just sellers to finish.

The Fed & the economy — Fed Tracker · Federal Reserve

The jobs report was hot: 165,000 jobs in October against roughly 70,000 expected, unemployment down to 4.1%, wages up 0.4% in a month. Good news for workers, bad news for anyone hoping for cheaper money. The Fed’s rate is 3.75–4.00% after a September hike. Futures now price about a 77% chance of another hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting, up from about two-in-three. The 10-year yield sits near 4.86%. No FOMC minutes or Beige Book came out this week. The October minutes arrive Nov 18. Tuesday’s CPI inflation report is next week’s biggest event.

Lesson of the week: Relative strength: who held up when the market fell

Relative strength compares a stock’s move to the market’s move. On a bad day, the stocks that fall the least are the ones big buyers refuse to sell. When the market recovers, those names usually lead.

  • Thursday: SPY: −4.4% (the market)
  • Thursday: HLT: −1.8% (held up)
  • Thursday: NVDA: −9.3% (sold hard)
  • Week: HLT vs SPY: +6.5 pts (HLT +3.8% vs SPY −2.7%)

Here’s the check: divide HLT by SPY. On Oct 30 it was 356.92 ÷ 755.72 = 0.472. Friday it was 370.45 ÷ 735.29 = 0.504. A rising ratio means HLT is beating the market. That’s why our long ideas are HLT and DAL, not NVDA. In a weak tape, buy the leaders, not the losers.

Plays for next week — Options Playbook

  • HLT Dec 18 $390 call — ≈ $645 · most you can lose. Why: the strongest trend on your list; the old high held Friday. Enter: a close above $381.34, or a hold of $362–364.50 that closes back over $370. Exit: a close below $359.41; targets $385.93, then $399.73. Delta 0.30. The bid-ask spread is wide ($5.60–7.30), so use a limit order near the middle.
  • DAL Dec 18 $85 call — ≈ $655. Why: an airline with cheaper fuel and a breakout in progress. Enter: a close above $88. Exit: a close below $83, or Brent back over $100; targets $91.86, then $95.18. Delta 0.61.
  • SPY Dec 18 $765 call — ≈ $634 · wait. Why: if the old floor is reclaimed, the selloff was a shakeout. Enter: a close back above $745, and not before Tuesday’s CPI. Exit: a close below $732; targets $757, then $765. Delta 0.27.

Skip this: Chip calls on Friday’s bounce: MU, AMD and SMH only fit the budget as long shots (delta under 0.20). Anything on NVDA held through its Nov 17 earnings. Dip-buying DELL, which your edge testing showed doesn’t work, with earnings Nov 24. New XOM or XLE calls while oil cracks. NOW puts after a 27% drop with RSI 28, which is too late. New trades Monday ahead of Tuesday’s CPI.

Your progress

  • Options basics so far: IV crush (Nov 1), why the market grades on expectations (Nov 2), delta (Nov 3), the trigger as a seatbelt (Nov 4), the 200-day line (Nov 5), and relative strength (today).
  • Fibonacci so far: the 78.6% line (Nov 5, NVDA) and role reversal (today, HLT). The ladders have also covered confluence and 3-point extensions along the way.
  • Next up: the Fib basics we skipped (picking the swing, retracements 101, shallow pullbacks, the golden pocket), and position sizing when the VIX is above 25.

Homework

  1. Mark $744–745 and $722–728 on your SPY chart. Watch how SPY reacts to Tuesday’s 8:30 a.m. CPI report at those two lines.
  2. Add HLT and NVDA to a comparison chart against SPY (Webull’s “compare” tool). See which line is rising.

Question: If CPI is hot and SPY drops to $725 Tuesday, which of the three plays would you still want, and which would you shelve?

Fib lesson of the week — Fibonacci Playbook (concept 6): Role reversal: HLT’s old ceiling became its floor

When price breaks above an old high, that high often becomes support on the way back down. Sellers who waited there are gone, and buyers who missed the breakout step in. It’s strongest when a Fib level sits at the same price.

The swing is the Sep 9 low at $300.00 (where this leg started) to the Nov 5 record high at $381.34. The old ceiling is the Oct 21 high at $364.50, which capped HLT until Monday’s close above it.

  • 23.6% retracement = 381.34 − (381.34 − 300.00) × 0.236 = 381.34 − 19.20 = $362.14
  • Old high = $364.50 → floor zone $362.14–364.50
  • Target: 0.786 extension = 335.23 + (364.50 − 300.00) × 0.786 = $385.93

Ladder (HLT):

  • $385.93 — 0.786 extension (target)
  • $381.34 — B · Nov 5 record high
  • NOW $370.45
  • $362–364.50 — Old high $364.50 + 23.6% $362.14
  • $350.27 — 38.2% retracement
  • $340.67 — 50% retracement
  • $335.23 — Oct 27 pullback low
  • $300.00 — A · Sep 9 swing low

Friday’s low was $364.54, 4 cents above the old high. HLT closed at $370.45. On Thursday, while SPY fell 4.4%, the low was $365.87, inside the same zone.

For a trade, the entry is a hold of the zone with a close back above $370. The stop goes just beyond the next level, not on it: a close below $359.41, about 1% under $362.14. The targets are $381.34, then $385.93.

Try it yourself: SPY’s old floor at $744–745 broke Thursday, and Friday’s high was $742.21. Watch whether that old floor now acts as a ceiling next week.
